brief:
King Abdullah of Jordan said the Middle East cannot achieve security until Palestinians gain their own homeland, Middle East Eye reported. The Jordanian monarch linked regional stability directly to resolving the Palestinian question, framing self-determination as a prerequisite for peace across the broader region.

Abdullah's statement reflects long-standing Jordanian positions on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, with Amman historically viewing a Palestinian settlement as essential to broader Middle Eastern security architecture.
dek: King of Jordan says no security in Middle East without Palestinian 'homeland' Jordan's King Abdullah has said there would be no security in the Middle East until the Palestinians' right to "their homeland" is fulfilled.
title: Jordan's king says Middle East stability hinges on Palestinian state
